question: After the output-loss race is fixed and final-head cross-platform proof is added, should OpenClaw adopt Execa 9.6.1 and its transitive dependency cone as the canonical core process backend?
rationale: This replaces a security- and availability-sensitive hand-rolled lifecycle at the root runtime boundary; code review can identify defects, but only the process/security owner can accept the permanent dependency and operational tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt after fixes
options.body: Land the Execa architecture only after repairing stream ordering and proving Linux and Windows success, failure, timeout, abort, and descendant-pipe behavior on the final head.

options.title: Narrow the migration
options.body: Keep Execa behind a smaller experimental caller set while the canonical wrapper and remaining raw-spawn paths retain current behavior.

options.title: Keep current backend
options.body: Decline the root dependency and standardize duplicated callers against the existing process wrapper instead.

recommendation.title: Adopt after fixes
recommendation.body: Land the Execa architecture only after repairing stream ordering and proving Linux and Windows success, failure, timeout, abort, and descendant-pipe behavior on the final head.

likelyOwner.reason: This account owns the linked direction and authored the security-sensitive dependency migration and process-contract preservation commits.
